top_story: Israel’s 12 November strike on Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, which killed a surgeon and five others and wounded 28 at one of Gaza’s last functioning medical sites, sharpened the sense that the war is collapsing the civilian infrastructure Palestinians rely on to survive. That pressure is now feeding Palestinian political debate inside Israel, where calls on 13 November for parties not to back Gadi Eisenkot reflect a view that reshuffling Israeli leadership without breaking war policy would offer Palestinian citizens little protection. The regional picture darkened further on 13 November when Iran claimed a retaliatory strike on a US radar site in Bahrain after a US attack on an Iranian communications tower, despite Washington’s denial that the sites were hit. The takeaway is a region moving deeper into militarised crisis, where attacks on essential civilian systems and the narrowing of credible political alternatives are reinforcing each other.
